answer_text:
Let  
\[
\beta=\sqrt[7]{3}
\]
and let \(\zeta_7=e^{2\pi i/7}\) be a primitive \(7\)th root of unity.

A root of
\[
f(x)=x^7+3
\]
is \(\alpha=-\beta\), since \(\alpha^7=-3\). Then all seven roots are
\[
\alpha\zeta_7^k=-\beta\zeta_7^k,\qquad k=0,1,\dots,6.
\]
Thus the splitting field is
\[
E=\mathbb{Q}(-\beta,\zeta_7)=\mathbb{Q}(\beta,\zeta_7).
\]

Now compute the degree.

First, \(x^7+3\) is Eisenstein at \(p=3\), so it is irreducible over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Hence
\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\beta):\mathbb{Q}]=7.
\]

Also,
\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7):\mathbb{Q}]=\varphi(7)=6.
\]

Since \(E\) contains both \(\mathbb{Q}(\beta)\) and \(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)\), the degree \([E:\mathbb{Q}]\) is divisible by both \(7\) and \(6\), hence by \(42\).

On the other hand,
\[
[E:\mathbb{Q}]
=[\mathbb{Q}(\beta,\zeta_7):\mathbb{Q}]
\le [\mathbb{Q}(\beta):\mathbb{Q}][\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7):\mathbb{Q}]
=7\cdot 6=42.
\]

Therefore,
\[
[E:\mathbb{Q}]=42.
\]

\[
\boxed{E=\mathbb{Q}\left(\zeta_7,\sqrt[7]{3}\right)\quad\text{and}\quad [E:\mathbb{Q}]=42}
\]
